business_problem: Cadence needed more flexible and secure compute capacity for electronic design automation workloads because chip-design demand, AI-enhanced tooling and tight time-to-market pressures outpaced what fixed data-center expansion could provide.
solution_summary: Cadence adopted IBM Cloud to support internal software development and EDA workloads that require large, burstable pools of secure compute. The company’s engineers run millions of jobs each month and need an environment that can shift massive workloads between on-premises systems and cloud resources without sacrificing project-level customization or security. IBM Cloud became the extension layer for those workloads, letting Cadence scale beyond the limits and procurement delays of its in-house data centers. In practice, EDA jobs and related development workloads can use cloud compute when local resources would bottleneck delivery, which is especially valuable as customers demand more sophisticated chip designs and shorter release cycles. The architecture is not just about capacity; it is also about enabling business agility, because access to elastic compute directly improves how fast Cadence and its clients can validate designs and bring new silicon to market.
